title: CTAB Genomic DNA Extraction Protocol
author: Michael Burgis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bwvjpe4n

steps.title: Prepare extraction and TE buffers
steps.instruction: Make 3 × Extraction buffer (autoclaved) containing 3 % CTAB (w/v), 1.4 M NaCl, 0.8 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 0.5 M EDTA pH 8.0, 3 M potassium acetate and 6 M NaCl; also prepare 1 × TE buffer (autoclaved) with 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 and 1 mM EDTA pH 8.0.

steps.title: Preheat buffer and add β‑mercaptoethanol
steps.instruction: Preheat the 3 × Extraction buffer in a water bath at 65 °C and add 0.3 % 2‑β‑mercaptoethanol immediately before use.

steps.title: Grind plant tissue and add buffer
steps.instruction: Grind 50 mg of plant material to a fine powder in liquid nitrogen using a pre‑chilled mortar and pestle; while still in the mortar add 800 µL of the pre‑heated 3 × CTAB extraction buffer and swirl gently with the pestle.

steps.title: Incubate lysate and cool
steps.instruction: Transfer the mixture to a 2‑mL microcentrifuge tube, incubate in a water bath at 60–65 °C for 1 h, mixing gently every 20 min by inverting the tube 20 times, then allow the tube to cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Add chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24 : 1 v/v) to the tube and mix by slight inversion.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with salts and isopropanol
steps.instruction: Estimate the aqueous phase volume (≈ 700 µL); add half of that volume (≈ 350 µL) of 6 M NaCl and mix well, then add 1/10 of the aqueous volume (≈ 70 µL) of 3 M potassium acetate while simultaneously adding 500 µL ice‑cold 100 % isopropanol (≈ 2/3 of the aqueous volume). Invert gently until DNA threads appear.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 M potassium acetate (1/10 aqueous volume).

steps.title: Centrifuge to pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 13 000 rpm for 15 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Transfer aqueous phase to new tube
steps.instruction: Using a wide‑bore pipette, carefully transfer the upper aqueous phase (which contains the DNA) to a fresh 1.5‑mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Repeat chloroform extraction until clear
steps.instruction: Repeat the chloroform:isoamyl alcohol addition (step 5) and aqueous‑phase transfer (step 6) until the upper aqueous phase is clear.

steps.title: Cold precipitation at –20 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at –20 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Spin and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 13 000 rpm for 5 min, then discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Drain residual supernatant
steps.instruction: Invert the tube containing the DNA pellet onto tissue paper to remove any remaining liquid.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in TE and incubate
steps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA pellet in 50 µL 1 × TE buffer and incubate at 50 °C for 1–2 h (overnight may be used for complete dissolution).

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL 70 % ethanol to the pellet, invert once to mix, then centrifuge at 13 000 rpm for 5 min.

steps.title: Discard ethanol and dry pellet
steps.instruction: Discard the ethanol, invert the tube on filter paper, and air‑dry the pellet at room temperature for 15 min (or incubate at 60 °C to speed drying).

steps.title: Assess DNA quality and quantity
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration and purity with a NanoDrop; typical yield is ~25 µg genomic DNA from 50 mg plant material.
